clue.text: Get lost, and propose hacking trees in Asian wilderness

parts.note: 'get lost!' is a brusque order to go away
to propose a price is to bid

indicators.note: hacking at the trees chops their letters up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to clear off proposes cutting down trees in an Asian wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacking' rearranges TREES into ESERT; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the vast arid region spanning Mongolia and northern China, a wilderness in Asia.

clue.text: Wound up Hungary flag

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: H is the international vehicle code for Hungary
to flag is to tire or droop, to sag

explanation.surface: Hungary's flag has been wound up a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as the past of wind, with 'up' joined to it; it is the noun, an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a long deep cut, a kind of wound.

clue.text: Interrupt delivery of pub drink

indicators.note: delivery here is the way words are spoken, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: a bar is a pub and gin a drink, so 'bar gin'

explanation.surface: Someone interrupts the delivery of a pub's drinks order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' looks like a lorry bringing stock; it is spoken delivery, so 'bar gin' said aloud gives the phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge in is to burst rudely into a conversation or room, cutting someone off.

clue.text: How this becomes his ultimate downfall?

definitions.text: How this becomes his ultimate downfall?

parts.words: How this becomes his ultimate downfall?
parts.note: cut the head (first letter) off the word 'this' and you get 'his'; for a person, losing the head is the final downfall

explanation.surface: A wry question about how a man meets his final ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, removing the T at the top of 'this' leaves 'his', and beheading is also a fatal end for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheading removes the head, both of a word's first letter and of a condemned man.

clue.text: Father obtains program foremost for housekeeping — it's a gem

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father
an app is a computer program

indicators.note: foremost for a word means its leading letter

explanation.surface: Dad gets a housekeeping app and declares it a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious blue stone, a gem.

clue.text: Casual joiner boards storage space

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory, storage space on a computer
'and' is a conjunction, a word that joins

explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter, but it is the grammar word AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random is haphazard or unplanned, as a casual choice is.

clue.text: Royal amongst paparazzi retreated

the letters sit amongst those of the word paparazzi

explanation.surface: A royal hiding among the photographers has drawn back.
explanation.definitionFit: Zara Tindall, granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II, is a member of the British royal family.

clue.text: Concentrate using a spanner?

parts.note: a bridge spans a gap, so it is a spanner

explanation.surface: A mechanic focuses hard on a job with a spanner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanner' is a wrench in the surface, but here it is anything that spans: BRIDGE; 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, concentrating it into fewer words.

clue.text: Individual tours parade after salt at bargain price

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, an AB (able seaman)

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the individual goes round the parade

parts.note: one is a single individual
a parade is a march

explanation.surface: A lone figure walks round a parade after something salty, picking up a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: À BON MARCHÉ is French, used in English, for 'cheaply'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means cheaply, literally 'at a good market', that is at a bargain price.

clue.text: Evergreen prizefighter, drained, intermittently punched in back

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the back

parts.note: the spine is the backbone, the back

indicators.note: a drained word has its contents emptied, leaving only its outside letters
taking letters at intervals, every other one, from the word punched

explanation.surface: An ageless boxer, exhausted, takes an occasional punch in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen' could describe the veteran boxer; it is the tree. 'drained' leaves PR, 'intermittently' gives UCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The spruce pine is a conifer of the American southeast that keeps its needles year-round.

clue.text: European city centre avoided by bear perhaps

indicators.note: the central letter of the bear's name is left out

parts.note: Bruno is a name given to many bears, real and toy

explanation.definitionFit: Brno is the second-largest city of the Czech Republic, in Moravia.

clue.text: Tight from booze in Tyneside — and more on the outskirts

indicators.note: the extra drink sits round the outside of the rest

parts.note: more booze, here mead, the old honey-based drink

spirits such as whisky are booze

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests drunk; it means stingy. Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight in the sense of miserly or stingy, ungenerous with money and spirit alike.

clue.text: At each entrance, lager's enjoyed around pub vault

indicators.note: the entrance to each word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A drinker enjoys lager in the pub before a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To vault is to jump over something, a leap.

clue.text: Cleaner out to lunch rejected liquid restraint

parts.note: 'out to lunch' is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.definitionFit: The Hoover Dam on the Colorado River holds back water, a restraint on a liquid.

clue.text: With technology company changing hands, call about a rise

indicators.note: the left hand, L, is changed for the right, R

parts.note: Apple is the technology company

parts.note: to cite someone, as a witness, is to call them

explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' looks like a sale; it swaps L for R in APPLE, giving APPRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets appreciate when they rise in value, so a rise is to appreciate.

clue.text: Film I swapped for one in French flat

explanation.definitionFit: A puncture in a tyre leaves it flat, and motorists call the mishap itself a flat.

clue.text: Make prized object, getting attention

parts.note: an end is an aim or object
to give an ear is to pay attention

clue.text: After term ends, summer in Nice attracts one for such a posh occasion?

explanation.walkthrough: Scottish term days were quarter days when leases ran out; Whitsunday was one.
explanation.definitionFit: White tie is the most formal evening dress code, demanded at grand, posh occasions.

clue.text: Area famous for 7 reflective spiritual books written by pen

a pen is an animal enclosure, a den or lair

explanation.walkthrough: 7 is the answer to 7 down, ABRIDGE, so the area is famous for a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto in Venice is a district famous for its bridge over the Grand Canal.

clue.text: High-flyer may pick up this fine on motorway, getting upset about it

explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' suggests a go-getter; here it is a frequent flyer collecting loyalty points.

clue.text: Joint beginning to languish in bath? Result of an accident perhaps

clue.text: Watery build-up in teeth, with front two missing, an endless stream

parts.note: the Ouse is a river, a stream

clue.text: A celebration opening associated with Watford's uplifting religious structure

clue.text: Retailer finally banned tumultuous crowd

clue.text: Plant metal outside in rain
